subject: microbiology
title: HIV, gp120, gp41, CD4, CCR5 and Reverse Transcriptase

steps.tx: **Human immunodeficiency virus** is an enveloped lentivirus with two copies of positive-sense RNA and enzymes including **reverse transcriptase**, integrase and protease. Surface **gp120** attaches to CD4 and a chemokine co-receptor, then gp41 drives membrane fusion. HIV 1 causes most global disease; HIV 2 is concentrated in West Africa, progresses more slowly and is intrinsically resistant to some antiretroviral classes.
steps.say: gp120 knocks on CD4, a co-receptor opens the door, and gp41 fuses HIV inside.

left.title: Entry sequence
points: Conformational change exposes co receptor site
gp41 inserts fusion peptide and membranes merge

right.title: After entry
points: Host transcription produces viral RNA and proteins

steps.tx: **CD4 receptor** expression targets helper T cells, macrophages and dendritic cells. CCR5 is the dominant co-receptor in transmitted infection; CXCR4-using variants may emerge later. People homozygous for CCR5 delta 32 are highly resistant to R5 HIV. Maraviroc blocks CCR5 and therefore requires a tropism test, while broadly neutralising antibodies and long acting agents target other vulnerable steps.
steps.say: CCR5 is the usual co-receptor at transmission, so tropism decides maraviroc's value.

right.title: X4 or dual tropic virus
points: Uses CXCR4 alone or with CCR5
Associated with faster CD4 decline in cohorts

steps.tx: **Reverse transcriptase** lacks proofreading, so HIV generates enormous diversity within one host. Combined with rapid turnover and recombination, monotherapy rapidly selects resistance. Antiretroviral therapy therefore uses multiple active drugs with a high barrier where possible. Integrated provirus in resting memory CD4 cells forms the latent reservoir that prevents cure by drugs alone.
steps.say: Error-prone reverse transcription makes combination therapy a mathematical necessity.

left.title: Diversity engines
points: Millions to billions of virions produced daily untreated
APOBEC and immune pressure add variation

right.title: Treatment implications
points: At least two or three active agents classically
Adherence prevents replicating virus under drug pressure

steps.tx: Acute HIV can cause a **seroconversion illness** with fever, rash, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy and mucosal ulcers two to four weeks after exposure. Viral load is very high and transmission risk is substantial. Fourth generation antigen antibody tests detect p24 and antibodies; HIV RNA resolves suspected acute infection when screening is negative or indeterminate. Early ART preserves immune function and prevents onward transmission.
steps.say: A mononucleosis-like illness after exposure plus very high HIV RNA is acute HIV until proven otherwise.

right.title: Immediate actions
points: Fourth generation test and HIV RNA
Start ART urgently after confirmation pathway

steps.tx: Transmission occurs through sexual contact, blood and from mother to child during pregnancy, delivery or breastfeeding. HIV is not spread by kissing, sharing food, mosquitoes or casual contact. A person with sustained **undetectable viral load on ART does not sexually transmit HIV**, summarised as U equals U. Prevention combines ART, PrEP, PEP, condoms, sterile injecting equipment and blood safety.
steps.say: Suppressed virus prevents sexual transmission; casual contact never transmits HIV.

nodes.label: No sexual transmission and better health

steps.tx: CD4 decline is driven by direct killing, chronic immune activation, lymphoid tissue damage and loss of mucosal integrity. Opportunistic diseases appear at characteristic CD4 ranges, but bacterial infections and tuberculosis can occur earlier. Viral load predicts replication activity and transmission, whereas **CD4 count estimates current immune vulnerability**. Both tests guide management, yet neither replaces assessment for tuberculosis and other active coinfections at diagnosis.
steps.say: CD4 measures immune damage; viral load measures the engine causing it.

left.title: CD4 count
points: Percentage can help when total varies

right.title: Viral load
points: Rising load triggers adherence and resistance review
Undetectable supports U equals U when sustained
